subject: RSNNS It always worked, however, today I used it and the forecast is very strange.

messages.subject: RSNNS It always worked, however, today I used it and the forecast is very strange.
parts:
Good afternoon.

I use the RSNNS package and today I noticed something strange. It always worked, however, today I used it and the forecast is very strange.

Do you know something? I am writing an article with this package.

require(RSNNS)
a<-jordan(scale(mtcars[,5]),mtcars[,1],  size=8, learnFuncParams = c(0.1), maxit=1000,linOut = TRUE)
b<-predict(a,data.frame(scale(mtcars[,5])))
plot(mtcars[,1],type="l",col="blue",ylim = c(1,40))
lines(b,type="l",col="black")
summary(a)
weightMatrix(a)
a<-mlp(mtcars[,5],mtcars[,1],  size=10, learnFuncParams = c(0.1), maxit=1000,linOut = TRUE)
b<-predict(a,data.frame(mtcars[,5]))
plot(mtcars[,1],type="l",col="blue",ylim = c(1,40))
lines(b,type="l",col="black")
--

Suellen Teixeira Zavadzki

Estatística - UFPR

messages.subject: Re: RSNNS It always worked, however, today I used it and the forecast is very strange.
parts:
Hi,

Please be more specific around what goes wrong, i.e., what would you expect the predictions to be in your example? What do you mean with "used to work"? Did this exact example produce different outputs in the past?

I've not changed anything in the package recently. Did you update it? Which version of RSNNS, which version of R have you been using before and after the observed change in behaviour?

On a different note, mtcars is not time series data, so running the jordan function on it doesn't make much sense. Also the plots you do suggest it is time series and they are potentially misleading, though they are ok to see that mlp seems to give a constant prediction. Have you tried to normalize the inputs before feeding it in?

Regards,
Christoph
